**My reasoning:**

I have been farming in Quzhou my whole life, and my family has about 5 mu of contracted land. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize — that rotation is what I know, what the market buys, and what the village grain station accepts. I would not try anything unfamiliar at my age with this land.

For wheat, I always plant in October after the maize comes off. I will use Jimai 22 seed again — the seed shop in town carries it and my neighbor has good results. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea at jointing. I water three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Last year aphids were bad so I will spray twice.

For maize I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June. I have been using Xianyu 335 hybrid for several years. I apply urea in two splits — at planting and at tasseling. Maize usually gets enough rain in summer but I irrigate once if it is dry around silking. One pesticide pass for borers is enough normally.

I keep a small strip of land near the house for vegetables — garlic, spinach, beans — just for the family table. I do not count that in my main plan.

I do not experiment. I follow what works.
